title: Image loading library (Kingfisher / Nuke style)
summary: A reusable SDK that loads, decodes, resizes and caches images for lists with zero hitches: request dedup, prioritization, cancellation, memory and disk caches, and progressive decoding.
requirements: Simple API for UIKit and SwiftUI; cancel on cell reuse.
No main-thread decoding; bounded memory; disk cache survives relaunch.
Prefetching, priority (visible first), placeholders, transitions, processors (resize, round corners).
components: Pipeline: request → memory cache (decoded, keyed by URL + processors + size) → disk cache (encoded data) → network
Task coalescing: one network fetch per URL, multiple subscribers
Decoding and downsampling on a background queue (ImageIO thumbnails at target pixel size)
Priority queue with limits (e.g. 6 concurrent downloads), priority updates when cells scroll
Disk cache with LRU by size and age, written atomically
tradeoffs: Caching decoded images is fast to display but memory-heavy; caching encoded data is compact but needs decoding again.
Separate cache entries per processed size avoid repeated work but multiply storage.
Using URLCache for disk is simple but less control over eviction and keys than a custom store.
body: **API:** `imageView.load(url, size:, placeholder:)` and a SwiftUI `LazyImage`; returns a cancellable task. Tasks are cancelled when the last subscriber cancels.
**Memory key:** URL + target pixel size + processor identifiers; avoids showing a tiny thumbnail when a large version is needed.
**Formats:** HEIC/AVIF/WebP support depends on OS; progressive JPEG rendering for slow networks; animated images decoded lazily frame by frame.
**Memory pressure:** NSCache auto-evicts; also purge on memory warning and when backgrounded.
**Staff angle:** SDK quality bars: thread safety documented, no global singletons forced on clients (allow custom pipelines), metrics hooks (cache hit rate, decode time), and binary size budget.
